review_reference: Coordinator's tasks of 17 Nov 2026 on hid-system#258 (Q94 way of working): port main 0089 (hid-system#73, 'keep the chosen facility across reload') onto staging as 0129, booked there; the design note on #258 and the decisions on it (STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE off | keep | ask, off by default; a failed read on GET /auth/session answers 200 with 'unavailable'; foreign keys to the sign-in, account, facility and membership, ON DELETE RESTRICT, as #262; the failure-audit fix is not part of this change). To be signed by the owner. Releases after 0124-0128; production's pending set is then exactly 0129.
evidence: Migration 0129_session_facility_selection.sql (sha256 db8e741ea61cba7de24ab94a836c0a4e005768351fbe0a24dcc2d16251512d8a) and its runtime-grants.sql block (file sha256 ab00882fe99cafafbba2e734ddf2d356baebab0b9535c4fd52ccbe8a21745db2). WHAT IT DOES: a new table auth.session_facility_selection, one row per staff sign-in (session family, keyed by family_id, the id of the family's first session; refresh keeps the family), with account_id, facility_id, membership_id, selected_at and row_version: the facility a staff member chose with POST /auth/facility, so a reload, a new tab or a refresh opens there instead of silently at the primary facility. Four foreign keys, all ON DELETE RESTRICT: auth.sessions(id), auth.accounts(id), identity.facilities(id), and identity.staff_facility_memberships(id, facility_id, account_id) through 0002's unique key (so the membership is the account's at that facility, and the demo and QA seals of 0098 and 0123 hold through it). No row-level security (like auth.sessions). The guard auth.guard_session_facility_selection_change() (plpgsql, SECURITY INVOKER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, every name qualified, revoked from PUBLIC, granted to no role) and its trigger session_facility_selection_guard (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE, FOR EACH ROW) refuse a delete and a move to another sign-in or account (55000 SESSION_FACILITY_SELECTION_IMMUTABLE) and admit a row only for the first session of a staff sign-in of that account with a live session (not revoked, not expired) at the account's current token version, an active account not disabled, and an active, unheld membership of that account at that facility with an active verified staff record, active organisation and active facility (else 23514 SESSION_FACILITY_SELECTION_INVALID): the staff context's own conditions. Grants, in the migration when the role exists and identically in runtime-grants.sql: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on the table to hid_identity_runtime (its API login inherits them); no DELETE or TRUNCATE; nothing to any other role or PUBLIC. No existing row, function, policy or grant changes. The row grants nothing: every facility-scoped request still carries X-Facility-ID, checked by the Identity guard, the access token has no facility claim, and identity-api re-checks the stored facility against the actor's current facilities for the session's own product on every read. NOT PORTED from main 0089: auth.lock_account_sessions (main 0073; the write locks the presented session FOR SHARE instead), the staff two-step sign-in (main 0088). DIFFERENCES from main: the guard also checks the account (active, not disabled) and the token version, uses search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, and the grants are made in the migration. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads, each a presence check; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0123 applied (0123's identity.sealed_qa_members); not yet applied (no table, guard or trigger of those names, else '0129: already applied'); every column the guard and the keys read, by name and type; the primary keys (id) of auth.sessions, auth.accounts and identity.facilities and the memberships' unique (id, facility_id, account_id), by exact column set; the applier owns, or inherits from the owner of, those four tables and may create in schema auth (42501). No earlier function is replaced or called, so there are no md5 pins of earlier bodies. POST-CHECKS: columns, keys and their actions, no row-level security, the guard's body (md5 f77032f5b5082fed66f7b01a3ee34f5a), attributes, owner and ACL, the trigger, the exact table privileges (the owner, and SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE, not grantable, to hid_identity_runtime when that role exists; any other grantee stops the file with the ACL in its message, whether or not hid_identity_runtime exists, because the role is compared null-safely: on a fresh install, before the roles are made, a default privilege to another role is refused as it is on an upgrade), and the guard fired once with random ids answering exactly 23514 SESSION_FACILITY_SELECTION_INVALID (its first run plans every query in it, so every column it reads exists). LOCKS: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.sessions, auth.accounts, identity.facilities and identity.staff_facility_memberships (the four foreign keys) and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the new table, held to commit (measured with pg_locks); taken first, NOWAIT, retried every 100 ms for at most 5 s, else 55P03 '0129: ... stayed busy for 5 seconds; nothing applied'. Reads are never blocked; sign-ins, refreshes, sign-outs and account or workforce changes wait until 0129 commits (applied in 15 ms recorded on the upgrade below; the table is new, nothing is scanned). BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: nothing reads or writes the table until identity-api runs with STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE keep or ask (infra HID_STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE, off by default); today's image, and the new image with the setting off, answer exactly as before. Turn the setting on only after 0129 is applied: with it on and the table or any of its three grants missing, identity-api refuses to start (the ECS deploy rolls back). The foreign keys add a check to deletes of sign-ins, accounts, facilities and memberships and to a change of a membership's id, facility or account; nothing on staging does either. TESTS: services/ehr-api/test/database/session-facility-selection.integration.sql (rollback-only, fictional data, through hid_identity_api_runtime): structure, privileges, the API's write (session FOR SHARE, upsert by family) and replacement, every refusal (patient sign-in, later session, another account's sign-in or membership, membership of another facility, signed-out or lapsed sign-in, ended or held membership, inactive or unverified staff, suspended facility, deactivated organisation, locked or disabled account, older token version, no sign-in), two roles at one facility, refused moves and deletes (the owner's too), rotation, sign-out, a facility suspended and an account disabled through the platform commands and a membership ended or held with a row present (all succeed, the same choice is then refused), and the demo and QA seals; and the sign-in as its family's first session (Rahman's review on #258): a family whose first session is a patient session or another account's, or whose only live session is a patient session or another account's, is refused even with a live staff session of the account in it, an account-only outreach session (Q88-2: a staff session of a verified staff login with no active membership) is refused directly and through the API's write, and a sign-in rotated twice, whose first session is revoked and whose third is live, makes its first choice (an INSERT) keyed to the revoked first session. PROVED 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18, for the file at the sha256 above, on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (fictional data only, deleted afterwards), schema owned and migrated by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS login (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds), runtime grants applied by the cluster superuser as security administrator: UPGRADE from staging 7831b440's 124 files (re-proved on 2026-11-18 after staging 7831b440, #265, was merged in; its migrations and runtime-grants.sql are those of 6364e4a1, where this was first proved) by staging's own runner, with staging's runtime-grants.sql and runtime-roles suite; then this branch's runner: plan exactly [0129] at the sha256 above; dry run rolled back (no table, 124 recorded); applied (execution_ms 15); 0 pending; the file again by psql answers '0129: already applied'; the migration granted exactly SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE to hid_identity_runtime (and through it hid_identity_api_runtime) and nothing else, and this branch's runtime-grants.sql then changed no runtime privilege (2477 before and after); bootstrap, --verify-only and the new suite pass. npm --prefix services/ehr-api run db:test-staging-upgrade (HID_REHEARSAL_ADMIN_URL, staging's runtime-grants.sql as the baseline): passed (baseline 124, integrated 125, declared [0129], dry run rolled back, checksums preserved, migration grants equal runtime-grants.sql over 2630 privileges, 206 tables' row-level security unchanged, the no-FORCE baseline, clean install). FRESH install of all 125 files, by the superuser and by the NOBYPASSRLS login: plan, dry run, apply, 0 pending, bootstrap and --verify-only pass. Database suites (96: 16 in database/tests, 80 in test/database): all 96 pass when the schema owner is the cluster superuser (as scripts/run-container-database-acceptance.sh builds it); 94 pass under the NOBYPASSRLS owner, where schema.integration.sql (RLS on ocr.job_events) and records-processing-draft.integration.sql (case 6n) fail exactly as they fail on staging 7831b440 without 0129. The new suite fails on 0001-0123 (the table does not exist) and passes after 0129; with the guard's body check lifted it also fails for each of 21 weakened guards (no token version, account status, disabled check, root session, revocation, expiry, hold, membership active, staff active, verification, organisation or facility active, membership account or facility, move or delete refusal, the first session's kind or account, the live session's kind or account, and a guard that wrongly requires the first session itself to be live). REFUSALS, each nothing applied (ledger 124, no table, guard or trigger): on 0001-0122, 55000 '0129: 0001-0123 must be applied first'; a login that is not the owner, and a NOINHERIT member of the owner, 42501; memberships.migration_hold_reason dropped, 55000 naming it; auth.accounts.token_version made integer, 55000 naming it; the memberships' unique (id, facility_id, account_id) dropped, or replaced by unique (id, facility_id), 55000; ROW EXCLUSIVE held on auth.sessions or on identity.staff_facility_memberships by an open transaction, 55P03 after about 5.2 s, while a third session's write on that table during the retries took 11 ms (no queue behind 0129); a copy of 0129 whose guard reads a column that does not exist (its md5 pin adjusted) passes section 0 and is stopped by section 5's firing (42703 reported), nothing applied; on a base with no hid_ role (a fresh install before bootstrap-database-roles), the migrator's default privilege on new tables in schema auth granting another role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE, DELETE, or SELECT WITH GRANT OPTION, 55000 '0129: the privileges on auth.session_facility_selection are not section 4's: ' and the ACL, and the same for SELECT with hid_identity_runtime present (a default privilege to PUBLIC is revoked by section 4, and 0129 then applies with only the owner, and hid_identity_runtime when it exists, in the ACL). Release checks: node scripts/verify-migration-ledger.mjs passes (125 migrations); npm --prefix release test and npm --prefix release run verify fail only with 'components config.migration.files: missing migration prefix', because 0124-0128 (#254, #255, #259, #262, #264) are not on this branch yet; with that gap tolerated in a throwaway copy of the verifier, verify passes. RECOVERY: 0129 is one file in one transaction (the runner's dry run of the pending set, then the file), so any stop (55P03 when the four tables stay busy, a precondition, a post-check) leaves nothing applied: production stays at its previous set, the plan is still exactly [0129], and the same release, with this declaration, can run again at a quieter time. This declaration lists only 0129, so a release whose pending set is anything else (for example 0124-0128 not yet released) is refused before anything runs (UNREVIEWED_PENDING_MIGRATIONS); release 0124-0128 first. ROLLBACK: an image rollback (production-backend-rollback changes images only) leaves the table, which older images ignore; to stop the behaviour, set HID_STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE to off (stored rows are then ignored). A forward migration can drop the trigger, the guard and the table (the rows hold only sign-in, account, facility and membership ids and a time; no clinical data).
